sources.name: Mara Vance
sources.quote: For me, accountability in 'The lives of C115: significant events and personal stories' comes down to being transparent about my own life and actions during that time. I've recently moved into a place of my own in Rockridge, which is a significant personal step. Professionally, I've been focused on my role as City Planning Director, and the directive I issued in C115 is part of that. I directed Avery Santana and Denise Carter to provide specific information and reconciliations related to petition responses and filings. I want to be clear that my actions are guided by a commitment to the principles of my office and the needs of the community.

sources.name: Howard Yell
sources.quote: I'm not sure what you're referring to about my living situation. I haven't moved recently, I've been living in Rockridge for a while now. It's a nice neighborhood, I've gotten used to the routine here.

sources.name: Xavier Robinson
sources.quote: The win at the window changed the week. I staked 365 and it paid 668. It's a nice boost, you know? I was just glad to have some good fortune. My kids are always on my mind, and it's nice to be able to treat them a little something extra.

sources.name: Imani Delacroix
sources.quote: I lost on the UNDOCKED book. It was a bad beat, but I've been down this road before. My slip came back empty, that's all. I'm not too shaken up about it.

limits.rule: The Packet is what you know, not the fence around what you may write. The approved facts and the ledger are canon: never contradict them, and never import real-world Oakland (its people, businesses, landmarks, troubles). Everything else — the scene, the street, the weather in the room, unnamed people and what they say, new in-world places and businesses, what the city is talking about — is yours to invent; that colour is the job, and it never rewrites a canon fact. A named ledger citizen speaks only in their approved quote or their own page line. Do not brief the record. Open on a person or place living the condition.

reviewProfile.purpose: Put the cycle's person events in the paper as news, one person at a time — a birth, a death, a hospital stay, a retirement, a promotion, a household set up or a place of one's own, a win or a loss on the book, what a turn of the city did to someone's day, and the smaller moments the record kept. The event is the lead, the person is named as the slice names them, and what came next appears only when a later record holds it. A stake or a payout is the person's own fact, not a statistic. The page is the city's real calendar; every person on it is one the record holds.

articleContract.voice: plain respect — a neighborhood weekly's births-and-obituaries hand, unhurried, exact
articleContract.opening: the heaviest event on the slice, stated as it happened to the named person
articleContract.closing: the last person's passage ends on what the record holds next for them, or on the fact itself — no moral, no roundup

authorizedTexture: the plain respect of the form — the ordinary weight of a birth, a retirement, a discharge, stated without ornament
the frame around a supplied fact — what a promotion to the supplied role means in plain words, without inventing the workplace
the neighborhood the slice names as where the person lives, without an invented street scene
the order and pacing of the passages — heaviest first, one person at a time
textureConditions: every person, event, role, employer, neighborhood, hospital stay, household and family tie must come from the slice
a quote appears only verbatim from the person's own supplied page; nothing paraphrased into quotation marks
what came next appears only when a later Cycle's supplied record holds it
a thin day (few events) is written as a short page, not padded
canonBlockers: any person, event, quote, venue, employer or family member not on the slice
a cause, diagnosis or outcome the record does not state
a statistic, rate or trend claim — the page is people, not numbers
intake bookkeeping rows (Emerged into Tier, Added to Simulation_Ledger, Updated to Tier) written as life events
raw engine labels or decimals printed as public-facing evidence
